decision: Generate and immediately evaluate a compact, stiff single-segment passive cantilever. The short backbone should make all ten bidirectional point-load cases settle with very small elastic motion, while the sole tendon remains safely slack because the legal passive payout greatly exceeds its route length.
evidence: The task requires all ten load cases in the single required condition all_load_cases, so the first evaluation must retain that complete condition.
The family permits one segment, length down to 0.015 m, Young's modulus up to 15000000 Pa, and rectangle dimensions up to 0.018 m by 0.018 m.
The mount points the backbone downward, and a 0.03 m segment remains far above the floor while reducing load moments.

Passive payout is at least 0.3 m; omitting an override preserves the 0.406 m default, leaving the approximately 0.03 m tendon route slack and avoiding unilateral-tendon preload or routing-induced bending.
A narrow 0.006 m z-height section leaves clearance for the tendon routed at 0.008 m, while the maximum 0.018 m y-width and maximum modulus provide strong bending resistance in the world-x load plane.

decision: Replace the invalid, effectively rigid one-segment c5 with a two-segment compliant beam whose terminal pose is passively restrained by four symmetric tendons; generate and immediately run the complete protocol on the new alias.
evidence: c5 completed stable unloaded and loaded windows with no contacts, but every load case was invalid because of ILLEGAL_TENDON_ROUTE_AT_CHECKED_POSES.

c5 moved only 5.39e-6 to 5.11e-5 m at the loaded point, far below the required 0.01 m, while its tip motion stayed below 0.000175 m; therefore substantially greater distributed compliance is needed without sacrificing terminal restraint.
c5 ratio values were 3.43 to 7.88 against a 0.3 limit, showing that a single tendon and one stiff segment do not create the required local-motion versus tip-motion separation.

A minimum-radius, minimum-modulus two-segment body should increase local deflection, while four evenly spaced terminal tendons provide bidirectional terminal restraint. A 0.007 m tendon radius remains outside the 0.003 m body and within payload and guide coordinate limits, improving route clearance relative to c5.
